entries.symptom: Validator asserts a historical/future vendor version label while authoritative integration evidence has changed.
entries.prevention: Assert capability, protocol and evidence semantics rather than brittle version prose.
entries.permanentGuard: development proof preflight + semantic integration validator

entries.symptom: A test reads a generated report/file that is not committed or packaged into the exact candidate.
entries.prevention: Proof reads the effective runtime registry directly unless the generated artifact is itself admitted and packaged.
entries.permanentGuard: preflight resolves every local new URL(..., import.meta.url) dependency before expensive proof

entries.symptom: Security fixture uses a retired source type alias not accepted by hardened runtime trust boundaries.
entries.prevention: Tests use canonical registered source families and fail if retired aliases reappear.
entries.permanentGuard: preflight retired-alias scan

entries.symptom: Test asserts an obsolete aggregate URL after the public artifact contract split into explicit video/caption/transcript URLs.
entries.prevention: Tests assert current public contract fields and no hidden compatibility field.
entries.permanentGuard: preflight stale artifact.url scan

entries.symptom: Later research overlay replaces nested verified evidence/value objects, silently losing prior mappings.
entries.prevention: Nested objects merge recursively while arrays remain explicit replacements.
entries.permanentGuard: preflight verifies mergePatch exists and rejects the retired shallow merge implementation

entries.symptom: Proof never reaches product/test execution because runner/builder allocation fails.
entries.prevention: Classify provider degradation separately, allow one controlled retry for a transient hypothesis, then exclude the degraded provider from pre-freeze capacity and route the exact SHA to a distinct executable failure domain.
entries.permanentGuard: pre-freeze provider-state admission + failure-domain proof-lane policy

entries.symptom: One failing capability or proof gate pauses unrelated development or downstream proof.
entries.prevention: Quarantine only the affected capability and explicit dependency scopes. Continue all unrelated development and proof stages; allow diagnostic-only progression for the blocked capability.
entries.permanentGuard: proof-stage router + control-plane isolation assertions

entries.symptom: An exact-image hosted proof service exists but lacks hosted-mode/database/public-origin/staging-credential prerequisites, so it can build successfully and fail only during startup or healthcheck.
entries.prevention: Read live lane configuration before freeze and require WFM_DB, WFM_HOSTED_STAGING, WFM_PUBLIC_ORIGIN and WFM_STAGING_PASSWORD; validate credential length and HTTPS origin in pre-deploy before the lane can count as capacity.
entries.permanentGuard: VECTOR_PRE_FREEZE_SIMULATION_V1 + Railway preDeploy full bootstrap contract

entries.symptom: A proof harness assumes one fixed loopback port and a fixed startup-attempt window, causing collisions or false runtime-start failures under loaded builders.
entries.prevention: Use ephemeral ports and condition-based readiness with a bounded diagnostic deadline rather than fixed sleeps/attempt counts.
entries.permanentGuard: pre-freeze readiness policy + collision-safe workflow runtime regression

entries.symptom: Multiple services on one provider are counted as independent resilience even though provider capacity/outage is a shared failure domain.
entries.prevention: Count independent failure domains rather than raw service/lane count. Same-domain workers may be added for throughput only when measured provider headroom exists; unknown/exhausted headroom routes to a distinct provider/domain.
entries.permanentGuard: pre-freeze failure-domain simulation + measured-headroom allocator + proof-lane policy validator

entries.symptom: Every development commit fans out expensive hosted proof and creates a self-inflicted provider queue.
entries.prevention: Coalesce development commits and trigger expensive hosted proof only on an explicit frozen-candidate artifact change.
entries.permanentGuard: artifact/vector-proof-freeze.trigger watch policy + freeze-only CI admission

entries.symptom: Final presentation composition gains a new admitted source but the provenance expected-source tree is not updated, causing late-stage hash/source failures.
entries.prevention: Bind every composed source into the provenance model and assert required source files exist before hashing.
entries.permanentGuard: built-asset provenance test + Docker source-tree existence checks

entries.symptom: A manually maintained service environment variable can lag behind the frozen commit and falsely appear to identify the candidate.
entries.prevention: Derive exact candidate identity from immutable freeze receipt, deployment commit metadata and source-bound build evidence; environment hints are never authoritative.
entries.permanentGuard: proof-lane candidate-identity policy + external deployment metadata comparison

entries.symptom: One frozen candidate automatically starts multiple same-scope/same-provider specialist and overflow builds, consuming shared build slots and delaying the proof stage that actually matters.
entries.prevention: Freeze triggers only the minimum canonical proof set; specialist/overflow services use lane-specific triggers and are activated only when the simulator assigns them.
entries.permanentGuard: proof trigger routing policy + Railway lane-specific watch patterns

entries.symptom: A lane can look green from commit status or domain configuration while the actual deployment was skipped, sleeping, failed, unreachable, or never bound to the exact candidate.
entries.learnedFrom: Railway exact-candidate Lane A and browser-proof admission audit 2026-09-25
entries.prevention: Require exact deployment SHA binding, public listen mode, sleep disabled, condition-ready health, outside-in endpoint reachability and an executable deployment state; SKIPPED/SLEEPING/status-only green never counts as proof.
entries.permanentGuard: VECTOR_PRE_FREEZE_SIMULATION_V1 execution-state + wake/reachability admission regression

entries.symptom: A newly created proof worker can start an initial deployment from a different branch/commit than the service configuration subsequently reports, so setup success can be mistaken for admissible evidence.
entries.prevention: Compare actual deployment branch/commit metadata with the intended proof-worker source before accepting any result. If create/redeploy reuses an old snapshot, reject it and trigger a watched source commit after live service config is correct.
entries.permanentGuard: proof-worker source-identity admission + deployment metadata comparison

entries.symptom: A browser proof worker can reach the exact hosted candidate and assets but receive HTTP 401 because its copied staging credential no longer matches the target proof runtime.
entries.prevention: Do not copy proof credentials across projects. Co-locate authenticated proof workers with the isolated target and use provider-native reference variables so secret rotation remains atomic and the secret never leaves the provider.
entries.permanentGuard: same-project provider reference for authenticated proof + login preflight before browser journey

entries.symptom: A proof harness can query an older review surface or omit the authoritative period and then miss state that was correctly persisted by the current workflow.
entries.learnedFrom: Time Review vs Weekly Review lifecycle proof alignment 2026-09-25
entries.prevention: Bind each proof assertion to the authoritative business source and explicit period/context; do not silently fall back to legacy aliases.
entries.permanentGuard: browser/action proof authoritative-source contract + watched verifier source

entries.symptom: A proof reads a visible-but-empty placeholder immediately after the network response and fails before the application finishes its authoritative refresh and renders the error.
entries.prevention: Wait for the semantic expected condition in the DOM or state, never element visibility alone when placeholders exist.
entries.permanentGuard: proof-lane policy semantic-observation rule + browser semantic wait regression

entries.symptom: A broad proof locator resolves multiple valid controls and strict-mode failure blocks the journey even though product behaviour is correct.
entries.learnedFrom: leave conflict modal Close/Cancel browser proof 2026-09-25
entries.prevention: Use unique accessible-name or source-bound locators and reject ambiguous proof selectors.
entries.permanentGuard: proof-lane policy unique-locator rule

entries.symptom: Provider healthcheck marks a proof worker healthy while the proof is still RUNNING, so infrastructure green can precede a terminal proof failure.
entries.prevention: Use a dedicated readiness endpoint that returns success only after terminal PASS; liveness and proof readiness are separate.
entries.permanentGuard: proof-lane policy terminal-readiness rule + /ready proof worker contract

entries.symptom: A developed capability and its tests exist on a specialist branch but are absent from the canonical convergence candidate, leaving a stale red proof lane and an incomplete product candidate.
entries.prevention: Canonical convergence must contain required runtime sources, hosted wiring and regression tests before freeze; specialist branches may not be the only copy of required capability.
entries.permanentGuard: canonical capability-completeness policy + Docker scheduling admission + hosted bootstrap wiring

entries.symptom: A newly wired hosted runtime service is present in the canonical source and Docker image but omitted from the local proof assembler, causing every exact proof lane to fail before hosted execution.
entries.prevention: Every absolute bootstrap dependency and each runtime service's relative dependency closure must be packaged by the local proof assembler and pinned by regression tests before freeze.
entries.permanentGuard: vector-runtime-packaging transitive scheduling closure + local runtime composer

entries.symptom: The proof readiness endpoint remains correctly fail-closed while the multi-role journey is still running, but the provider diagnostic health deadline expires before the proof can reach terminal PASS.
entries.prevention: Keep readiness semantic and condition-based; set the provider diagnostic ceiling above the measured proof runtime and fail immediately on terminal proof failure rather than on arbitrary attempt counts.
entries.permanentGuard: dedicated /ready terminal-PASS contract + Railway browser proof diagnostic ceiling
